 SCHUYLKILL COUNTY, Pa. - Former U.S. Congressman and Chairman of the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board, Tim Holden, has passed away at 69 years old.
 According to a social media post, Holden died on Sunday, November 15. His cause of death has not yet been released.
 Holden began his career as Schuylkill County’s Sheriff before making a move and representing Pennsylvania in Congress for 20 years from January 1993 to January 2013. He served for a total of ten consecutive terms.
 The Pottsville City Democratic Committee posted a statement on his passing on social media, saying they are grateful for his many years of service and dedication to the people and communities he represented.
 The committee said his roots in the community will remain an important part of the area’s history.
 The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board also released a statement about his death, saying he was a “dedicated public servant and a tireless advocate for the people of Pennsylvania.”
 “During his 11 years with the PLCB, he provided steady leadership, helping guide us through changing and often challenging times,” the statement read.
 “More than that, Tim was a friend, someone who could always be counted on to listen and offer wise advice shaped by his years of political, congressional, and personal experiences,” the PLCB went on to say.
 Additionally, Gov. Josh Shapiro posted about Holden’s death on X Sunday night, calling him a “good man and a true public servant who never forgot where he came from.”
 “Lori and I are praying for Tim’s loved ones. May his memory forever be a blessing,” Gov. Shapiro’s post read.
 Tim will be deeply missed by many in the community.
